items.title: CHOREO reports long-horizon composition of heterogeneous humanoid skills through a shared trajectory interface

items.content_text: BarrierFormer trains a causal transformer to predict short state rollouts and enforce control-barrier constraints through a training-time safety teacher, removing online optimization at inference. The authors compare it with four reimplemented baselines across a double integrator, Dubins car and Crazyflie simulator, using 32 environments and three seeds. Their learned-dynamics variant reports 95.83%–96.88% safety on two 2D systems and 96.88% on the 3D system, with per-step batched inference around 4.79–5.12 microseconds on one workstation. This is a simulation result: training still uses a black-box simulator, performance degrades as complexity rises, and the authors warn of a potentially large simulation-to-real gap.
items.title: BarrierFormer reports predictive safety control with low simulated inference latency

items.content_text: The authors present EgoWild2Dex, which aligns egocentric human observations with robot views and trains a dexterous manipulation policy through broad human-data pretraining, task-specific human–robot co-training and robot-domain refinement. Their EgoWild corpus contains 538.9 hours, 179,049 episodes and 125,961 task descriptions. On three long-horizon bimanual tasks, the authors report 90%–100% success using less than one hour of robot demonstrations per task; object-level success on three unseen package contents is 30%–40%. GeoFormer image alignment is reported at 7.43 ms mean latency versus 162.58 ms for a projection-and-inpainting baseline, excluding image decoding and model loading. These are author-reported results from a limited task and robot setting; the paper says the data, models and code will be released and still requires robot fine-tuning.
items.title: EgoWild2Dex reports transferring in-the-wild human video to bimanual robot manipulation with limited robot data

items.content_text: The authors combine a closed-loop engineering-change-order workflow with a Qwen3.5-9B model trained on repair demonstrations and action preferences. Across 22 chip designs and 594 runs, they report a mean repair score of 79.65 for INT8 and 79.63 for BF16, versus 77.44 for GPT-6 Astra under a shared execution protocol. Their cost model estimates INT8 inference at $0.00226 per task versus $0.33188 for GPT-6 Astra, about 1/147 as much, excluding EDA and idle costs. These are author-reported results from one benchmark; nine designs are held out, but the broader generalization and deployment economics remain unverified.
items.title: WaveletECO reports a specialized local model matching a frontier API on chip-repair scores at lower estimated inference cost

items.content_text: The authors introduce FoldQuantVLA, which keeps activation coordinate transforms consistent across calibration, quantized weight rounding and TensorRT execution. On GR00T N1.5/N1.6/N1.7 and π₀.₅, they report W4A4 projection speedups of 1.20–1.33× over floating-point TensorRT on Jetson AGX Orin and 1.25–1.52× on a desktop RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. A selective W8A8 setting for two language projections adds 1 ms to the N1.7 Orin path and reports 92.5% pooled success versus 80.0% for uniform W4A4 across 80 physical-robot trials. These are author-reported measurements: selective-precision gains were not resolved in their LIBERO controls, robot trials were small, and latency measurements used one timing run.
items.title: FoldQuantVLA reports faster low-bit inference for vision-language-action policies with small-task robot results

items.content_text: Apple’s Sept. 22, 2026 newsroom update makes Mac Studio systems with M5 Ultra available and lists configurations with up to 512 GB unified memory and 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth. Apple also says Thunderbolt 5 with RDMA enables multiple Mac Studio systems to deliver up to 3× the distributed-inference performance of one system. The product specifications and release are first-party facts; the speedup is an Apple claim whose exact model, cluster size, metric and power/cost basis are not specified in the inspected page. No independent benchmark or matched cost analysis was performed.
items.title: Apple introduces a 512 GB M5 Ultra desktop and claims faster RDMA-cluster inference

items.content_text: Zhang et al. present Conduit, an Experience Data Plane that separates reinforcement-learning experience ingestion, placement and delivery from framework execution. The authors report up to 97% lower exposed experience-path latency and up to 38% lower end-to-end iteration latency in RLlib tests spanning DQN, SAC and PPO workloads on an eight-actor/eight-learner setup. They also report scaling from 8 to 1,024 AMD MI250X GPUs on a fixed workload, compared with Conduit without adaptive placement, and similar convergence curves in two tested tasks. These are author-reported results from one preprint, not an independent reproduction; transfer to other workloads and full cost/energy effects remain unmeasured.
items.title: Conduit turns distributed RL experience handling into a runtime optimization surface

items.content_text: EDGEGEN extracts compliance rules from an agent specification, combines structured rule-violation scenarios with executable database states, and uses the generated tasks for fine-tuning or harness optimization. The authors report improvement over the base model in all 18 model–benchmark comparisons across three benchmarks; on tau2-bench Airline they report relative mean-progress gains ranging from 2% to 42%, while one harness-optimization result for Gemma-4-e4b is 10% above human-curated and 30% above the base harness. Main evaluations use only 10–15 scenarios per benchmark. In a small audit, human reviewers confirmed only 6 of 10 Airline and 4 of 10 ToolSandbox runs labeled successful. These are preprint-reported results, not independently reproduced evidence of general agent reliability.
items.title: EDGEGEN reports gains from specification-derived edge-case tasks for tool-calling agents

items.content_text: GLIDE is a framework that generates executable command guardrails from task descriptions, refines them using teleoperation trajectories and reuses them during policy execution. Across three dual-arm manipulation tasks, the authors report that GLIDE guardrails raise teleoperation success to 70%, 90% and 90%, compared with 0%, 10% and 0% under unguarded teleoperation and 20%, 60% and 60% under domain-expert hardcoded guardrails. In 10-trial policy conditions, runtime guardrails improve two success-only-trained tasks but reduce wine-serving success from 50% to 40%; mixed-quality GLIDE data with filtering reaches 70%, 60% and 60%. The paper reports a bounded physical-robot study, not general safety or broad task transfer. The authors provide a public runtime repository and demonstration datasets, which were not independently run or analyzed here.
items.title: GLIDE reports that executable guardrails improve manipulation demonstrations and selected robot-policy trials

items.content_text: BackTrend is a retrospective benchmark built from 25 mature AI/ML topics and 66 human-validated early problem- and solution-space signals, with systems restricted to evidence available by the end of 2023. Across seven evaluated LLM, RAG and agentic systems, the authors report maximum semantic-judge F1 of 10.1% and Coverage@10 of 18.5%; deeper retrieval helps some systems, while unlimited search can reduce performance. In a sample of 100 unmatched predictions, two annotators judged 49% and 57% plausible, suggesting the reference set may omit valid signals and benchmark F1 can understate performance. The authors report a useful retrospective evaluation result, not evidence that current systems have or lack prospective scientific foresight.
items.title: BackTrend reports that current research agents recover few validated scientific weak signals in a retrospective benchmark

items.content_text: A September 21 arXiv paper introduces a multimodal traversability estimator trained from about 500 sols and 45 km of Mars 2020 Perseverance driving data. On 35 held-out sols, the authors report AUROC 0.874, average precision 0.878 and F1 0.758, above the strongest listed baseline (0.816, 0.802 and 0.602); means are reported across five seeds. They also describe integrating the learned hazard map into modified ENav flight software and testing it on an Earth-analog rover, primarily on flat ground with large rocks. These are paper-reported results. The linked project page says code and dataset are forthcoming; no independent reproduction or Mars deployment is established.
items.title: Perseverance driving data supports paper-reported multimodal traversability learning on an Earth-analog rover

items.content_text: DUMA-Bench introduces executable security scenarios in which an agent and user simulator can both shape a changing environment. The paper reports higher attack success under dual-control than solo evaluation (41.1% vs 26.9%), but the linked repository README currently displays 40.3% vs 25.4% over 1,960 trials per regime. That paper–artifact difference has not been reconciled. The comparison also changes multi-turn interaction, user activity and environment evolution together, so it is a regime-level robustness gap rather than an isolated causal estimate of user influence. State assertions are deterministic, while communication assertions use GPT-4o judging.
items.title: DUMA-Bench reports higher agent attack success in dual-control tests, with a paper–artifact mismatch

items.content_text: The Sep. 21 arXiv paper analyzes paired, event-keyed environment schedules for group-relative reinforcement learning of tool-using agents. Its theory shows that pairing removes the shared environment-noise component from sibling reward contrasts but can still increase gradient variance under some score geometries. In a registered study using one Qwen3.5-2B agent and three seeds per design, pairing improved noisy-test success under transient tool faults by 5.1 points but missed the registered learning-curve criterion; under grader flips, the learning-curve difference was small and uncertain. A finite probe found lower gradient covariance traces, but the result is limited to eight checkpoints from two trajectories and does not establish broad learning gains.
items.title: Paired rollout schedules reduce reward noise, but do not guarantee better agent learning

items.content_text: NVIDIA's Sep. 22, 2026 Isaac ROS 5.0 materials add agent-ready robotics workflows and describe using an AI-guided skill to migrate a Depth Anything 3 TensorRT node to ROS 2 Lyrical's rosidl::Buffer with a CUDA backend. ROS 2 documentation supports buffer-backed uint8[] message fields, while the upstream CUDA backend README describes same-host/same-GPU/same-user IPC and CPU fallback elsewhere. NVIDIA's tutorial presents an implementation and a verification recipe, but this review found no measured end-to-end performance result for that node migration.
items.title: NVIDIA pairs an agent-guided ROS 2 migration workflow with buffer-backed GPU transport

items.content_text: Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen compare OpenAI’s natural-language Navier–Stokes proof with cited Lean declarations. For Lemma 8.6, equation (8.19), they report that the manuscript states an m+4 derivative estimate while the cited Lean estimate requires m+5. For pressure-flux equation (10.19), they report a different Lean bound and proof route, including an additional localized gradient norm. They note one similar auxiliary bound in the repository does not appear to be directly used in the proposed theorem, leaving the effect on the actual proof dependency chain unresolved. The authors explicitly do not claim the natural-language blow-up proof is incorrect. This remains a source-reported critique in an arXiv preprint, without independent reproduction or established specialist consensus.
items.title: A mathematical-analysis preprint reports mismatches between OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof and cited Lean estimates

items.content_text: EvoOntology presents an MCP-served ontology that data agents can query at runtime and refine through typed edits admitted only after paired evaluation on held-out tasks. On three data-agent benchmarks, the authors report improvements over no-ontology baselines across multiple backbones. On DDR-Bench, the paper reports a mean Trajectory-Wise gain of 12.3 percentage points from the initial ontology and another 7.7 points after self-evolution; on BIRD, initial ontology improves execution accuracy by 5.1 points and evolution adds 3.7. In an ablation averaged across four backbones, removing the paired gate lowers the final DDR-Bench score from 89.5 to 78.3 (-11.2 points), the largest drop among four loop components. These are author-reported results from a single preprint; no independent reproduction is reported here.
items.title: EvoOntology reports gains from queryable semantic state and a regression-blocking evolution gate

items.content_text: The Cache-to-Cache (C2C) paper proposes transferring a source model’s key/value cache into a target model through a learned fuser, bypassing text generation between models. Across four question-answering benchmarks and several Qwen, Llama and Gemma combinations, the authors report 6.4–14.2% higher average accuracy than individual models and about 3.1–5.4% above text-to-text handoffs; latency was 2.5× faster on average in their tested settings. Their detailed timing table reports 3.46×, 1.51× and 14.41× speedups over text handoff for three model pairs. The fuser uses trainable pair-specific components, and scaling to many communicating models with O(N) training cost remains open. These are paper-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.
tags: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
items.title: Cache-to-Cache reports faster cross-model communication through direct KV-cache transfer

items.content_text: On Sept. 18, 2026, Anthropic announced a non-exclusive partnership with Accenture’s Faculty business to evaluate and red-team models, assess alignment, and test safeguards. Each organization said it expects to invest at least $1 billion over five years to build capacity. Evaluators are intended to work inside AI companies with access comparable to employees, including observation of training and deployment decisions and direct staff interviews. Anthropic said access and reporting standards, and a settled funding model for independent evaluation, do not yet exist; it will directly fund this partnership while exploring pilots with nonprofit evaluators. This is evidence of an announced organizational model and planned investment, not evidence that evaluations are operating or independent in practice.
items.title: Anthropic and Accenture announce a directly funded embedded evaluation partnership
